slides.text: Narayana's chai stall. 5 AM. Thirty years.
He knew every order by heart. Strong for the auto drivers. Extra sugar for the students.
One old man came every day. One chai. Same corner. Always alone.
One morning he didn't come. Nor the next. On the third day, Narayana shut his stall early.
He carried a flask to the old man's house. Fever. Nobody else had noticed.
"When your chai goes undrunk, I know something is wrong." Some relationships don't need a name.
